findings.text: - [P1] Initialize the new field in the candidate solve path — crates/bifrost-policy/src/taint_policy.rs:382. The production candidate solver also constructs `PreparedTaintPlan` in `taint_policy/candidate.rs`, but that initializer does not supply `sink_files`. Because the candidate module is compiled unconditionally, this change makes `bifrost-policy` fail to compile with a missing-field error, blocking all builds that depend on it.

- [P2] Preserve coverage of the shared scan budget boundary — crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/semantic_model/callable_values.rs:277-279. When the fact scan consumes the last allowed record before coverage collection begins, the removed test was the only check that the query reports `RecordBudgetExhausted` and does not claim complete coverage. The retained test has enough budget for both phases, so it cannot catch a regression at this boundary; this is the kind of tricky edge case the repository explicitly retains tests for ([AGENTS.md:128](AGENTS.md#L128)).

- [P2] Preserve coverage for a budget exhausted between query stages — crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/semantic_model/callable_values.rs:278 — When the final allowed record is a matching fact and a coverage record remains, the shared budget must prevent the coverage claim from being returned and report `RecordBudgetExhausted`. The deleted test was the only check of that cross-stage boundary; the retained test has ample budget, so resetting the counter before coverage would silently turn a bounded result into an apparently complete one. This is the kind of tricky boundary for which [AGENTS.md:128](AGENTS.md#L128) calls for a test.

- [P1] Restore formatting before the CI format check — crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/semantic_model/callable_values.rs:375 — Removing the final test leaves its indented closing brace as the module's closing brace, so `cargo fmt --check` fails in the required CI formatting job. The same issue occurs in `catalog/mod.rs`, and the deletions also leave extra blank lines in several files.

- [P1] Restore rustfmt-compliant module closures crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/semantic_model/callable_values.rs:375: Removing the last test leaves its indented closing brace as the module's closing brace; the same issue occurs in `catalog/mod.rs`. `cargo fmt --check` rejects these files, so the formatting job in CI fails on this change. The repository's [Rust validation guidance](.agents/docs/testing-and-rust-validation.md#L134-L140) requires formatting before the pre-push gate.

- [P2] Retain the initialization retry deadline test — crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/semantic_model/catalog/db.rs:734 — If SQLite continues returning a retryable BUSY or PROTOCOL error until the deadline, initialization must stop retrying and return that error. The removed test was the only one exercising expiration; the remaining retryable-error test eventually succeeds and the LOCKED test takes a different branch, so a regression could leave catalog opening stuck indefinitely under persistent contention. The deadline is a tricky timing boundary covered by [AGENTS.md:128](AGENTS.md#L128).

- [P2] Retain the initialization retry deadline check — crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/semantic_model/catalog/db.rs:733-735. When SQLite continues to return a transient error until the deadline, the removed test was the only check that initialization stops retrying and returns that error. The remaining tests cover eventual success and a non-transient error, so an unbounded retry under persistent contention would go undetected; the repository calls for tests of tricky conditions ([AGENTS.md:128](AGENTS.md#L128)).
